messages:
maria_cust: hi — hitting a wall with 429s after we turned on extended context (trying to use ~80k tokens). traffic pattern is bursty: ~10–15 rps sustained bursts for 30s every 5m. model is rwd3-64k. errors started after we switched from 8k context to 64k. stack: node client calling /v1/generate. sample curl that fails: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \\
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxx' \\
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
  -d '{"model":"rwd3-64k","input":"<long prompt...>","max_tokens":2048}'
```
we see: 429 Too Many Requests and sometimes high p95 latency (~1.2s vs usual 200ms). any guidance?

alex_support: hey maria — thanks for the details. a couple quick qs: when you say 10–15 rps bursts, is that across many client instances or a single client? do you have request/response headers from failed calls (Retry-After, X-RateLimit-*)? can you paste a raw failing response?

maria_cust: single service fanout to api (many threads inside our app) — effectively many simultaneous connections. here's a raw failing response we captured:
```json
{
  "error": "429 Too Many Requests",
  "message": "per_model_rpm_exceeded",
  "retry_after": 22
}
```
and one example response header we logged:
```
Retry-After: 22
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1717689130
```
(sidenote: the client sees intermittent 504 on a few calls during the same windows)

jamie_sre: thanks — this looks like classic per-model throughput + context token cost interaction. short expl: rwd3-64k has a per-model RPM/TPM budget and a separate max concurrency threshold. long-context requests consume many more token budget (both input + output tokens count toward TPM), so even modest rps with big contexts can hit TPM quickly. bursts can also trip the RPM burst window if you hit many requests within the short burst interval.

jamie_sre: quick checklist for repro & triage:
- confirm per-client concurrency (open sockets) — many parallel connections can exceed the model's max_concurrency.
- measure tokens/request (input_length + expected output) to estimate token/sec load vs model TPM.
- capture response headers (Retry-After, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset).
- check dashboard metrics: per-model rpm, tpm, concurrent_sessions during the incident window.

maria_cust: we looked at token counts — avg input ~60k tokens, output ~1500 tokens per request. that explains a lot. any immediate mitigations besides throttling?

eng_inference: some options (ordered from fastest to more involved):
1) client-side rate limiting: implement a leaky-bucket token bucket and concurrency cap. cap simultaneous open requests to the model's max concurrency reported in your plan (we can share the exact number for rwd3-64k). add jitter and exponential backoff when you see 429s.
2) reduce context: try pipelining or truncating old context, store long history in a vector DB and only fetch the top-K relevant chunks instead of sending full 60k.
3) switch to a cheaper/less-constrained variant for non-critical calls (e.g., rwd3-8k or rwd3-16k) and reserve rwd3-64k for the few requests that truly need long context.
4) request a quota bump / dedicated capacity: Dedicated pools remove most shared per-model throttles and give predictable concurrency.
5) enable prefix/KV caching if your workload has repeated prefixes. caching can reduce token decode work and avoid repeated TPM cost for shared prefixes.

alex_support: i'll also add common pitfalls we see:
- underestimating token cost: input + output both count. streaming still counts.
- mistaking RPM for TPM: you might appear under RPM but still hit TPM because of huge contexts.
- client-level retries without jitter: spikes multiply and bring a spike storm.

maria_cust: we saw Retry-After values ~20–30s repeatedly. what's the burst window behavior? we thought bursts would be allowed.

jamie_sre: burst behavior: there's a short burst window for RPM (small leaky bucket) intended to absorb brief spikes (few seconds). longer bursts (tens of seconds) are throttled against sustained RPM/TMP and concurrency caps. when you exhaust the bucket you get 429s with retry_after roughly equal to seconds until reset. also TPM limits may be enforced continuously and can throttle high-token requests even with RPM available.

maria_cust: can you confirm headers we should rely on? we saw X-RateLimit-* but sometimes it's missing on 504s.

eng_inference: rely on Retry-After when present for 429s. X-RateLimit-Remaining is useful but can be eventually consistent. 504s are edge-timeouts — collect request IDs and timestamps and we can correlate with the infra logs. include the request-id header (if present) and the full body/size.

maria_cust: repro steps I can share quickly:
1) run 12 parallel clients each issuing requests every 1s with 60k token input and 1500 token output target.
2) observe 429s in ~30–90s window, Retry-After returned ~20s.
3) lower to 3 parallel clients or truncate to 8k context => errors disappear.

jamie_sre: perfect reproduction. next steps from our side:
- alex_support: can you escalate to eng_inference with sample request-ids and a 10m window around 1717689000–1717689300?
- eng_inference: please check per-model throttle logs, token accounting and the concurrency circuit for that tenant.
- billing_ops: flag customer for potential Dedicated offer — large extended-context usage can be cost-inefficient on shared capacity.

alex_support: done — attaching captured request-ids and a short CSV of timestamps in the escalation ticket. deploy-bot: note for oncall routing.

deploy-bot: incident note created: INC-2026-1717689000 — routing to eng-inference + SRE.

eng_inference: quick findings (initial): we see the tenant hitting ~18k input tokens/sec which maps to ~1.1M tokens/minute — above the shared TPM for rwd3-64k. concurrency also hit the per-tenant session cap briefly. we'll pull kernel-level logs to confirm queueing and export the exact limits to the support ticket.

eng_inference: temporary workaround we've applied: flagged the tenant for automatic short-term throttling to smooth bursts (soft cap) and increased the retry header to encourage longer backoff. this should reduce 429 frequency while we consider capacity options.

maria_cust: thanks — we'll implement client concurrency cap and prefix trimming ASAP. can you provide the exact numbers for rwd3-64k (RPM, TPM, max concurrency, burst window length) so we can tune our client?

eng_inference: will share exact numbers in the ticket (we redact per-plan limits in public channels). rough guidance meanwhile: assume TPM is the binding constraint for 60k-context workloads; plan for token-budgeted throttling and keep concurrency <= 8 for this model unless on Dedicated.

alex_support: checklist for you to avoid recurrence:
- cap concurrent requests per model (<=8 as a starting point)
- implement token-aware rate limiting (count input+expected output)
- exponential backoff with jitter on 429s (respect Retry-After header)
- consider split/compact history or vector DB approach to keep context smaller
- if usage is steady and business-critical, open a Dedicated capacity conversation with billing_ops

maria_cust: great, appreciate the clear next steps. i'll update the ticket once client changes are live and post reprod results.

jamie_sre: thx — if you still see 429s after reintro, ping here with fresh traces and request-ids. we can also run a quick smoke test from our side to verify smoothing.

maria_cust: will do. :thumbsup:
